text: In the United States, a principal told English teacher Lee McCarthy that Gabriel García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude could no longer be used in school. McCarthy filed a lawsuit in 1986 against school administrators and Wasco Union High School District's Board of Trustees, and the book was deleted from the 1986–1987 school year curriculum. In Kuwait, a ministry censorship committee blacklisted the novel; a report said it was banned because of a scene in which a wife saw her husband naked.
meta_description: One Hundred Years of Solitude by Gabriel García Márquez: deleted from a school curriculum for 1986–1987 and blacklisted by a Kuwaiti censorship committee.
changes: Reordered chronologically (1986 before Kuwait); lawsuit and curriculum deletion kept together.
